# test_is_valid_email.py

# Replace `your_module` with the actual name of the module that contains

# These tests use `pytest` style and cover happy-path, edge-case, and

import pytest
from your_module import is_valid_email


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy-path (clearly valid addresses)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "address",
    [
        # Simple canonical address
        "user@example.com",
        # Mixed upper/lower, digits and underscore
        "USER_123@test-domain.co",
        # Local part with dot, plus, underscore, hyphen; multi-level domain
        "first.last+category@sub.domain.co.uk",
        # Smallest allowed components (one char either side of @, 2-letter TLD)
        "a@b.cd",
        # Mixed case in TLD
        "local@domain.CoM",
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_happy_path(address):
    assert is_valid_email(address) is True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edge-cases that are still supposed to be invalid
# (boundary lengths, whitespace, etc.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "address",
    [
        "",                             # empty string
        " ",                            # whitespace only
        "user@domain.c",                # TLD only 1 char
        " user@domain.com",             # leading space
        "user@domain.com ",             # trailing space
        "user @domain.com",             # space inside local part
        "user@ domain.com",             # space inside domain part
        "two..dots@domain.com",         # consecutive dots in local part
        "user@domain..com",             # consecutive dots in domain
        ".startswithdot@domain.com",    # leading dot in local
        "endswithdot.@domain.com",      # trailing dot in local
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_edge_cases(address):
    assert is_valid_email(address) is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clearly invalid formats / characters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "address",
    [
        "plainaddress",             # missing @
        "missingatsign.com",        # still missing @
        "@missinglocal.com",        # missing local part
        "missingdomain@.com",       # domain missing before dot
        "missingdot@domaincom",     # no dot between domain & TLD
        "user!@domain.com",         # illegal character in local
        "user@domain.123",          # numeric TLD
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_error_cases(address):
    assert is_valid_email(address) is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Non-string inputs should raise because `re.match` requires str/bytes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [None, 123, 12.34, ["list"], {"dict": 1}])
def test_is_valid_email_non_string_input_raises(bad_input):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        is_valid_email(bad_input)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
